cards.text: Jesus has just finished praying to the Father for His disciples (John 17). Now He goes out with them across the Kidron Valley, and they enter a garden. Friend, grab your apron and hold on, because this is where the story turns.
There's just one problem with this garden. Judas, His betrayer, knows the place too.

cards.question: Why does Judas, the one betraying Jesus, know this garden?

answers.text: Jesus had often met there with His disciples
The chief priests had shown him the way there
His family had once owned the land nearby

cards.text: So Judas shows up, and he does NOT come alone. He brings a band of soldiers, plus officers, and friend, when I need help moving an oven, I can't get TWO people to show up.

cards.question: Judas brings officers along with the soldiers. Who are the officers from?
Judas and the crowd arrive at the garden carrying lanterns, torches and ___.

cards.text: Lanterns, torches, weapons, and more light than I saw in all my years in the back of that junk drawer. And Jesus? He knows all that is coming upon Him.

cards.question: The crowd is coming into the garden, and Jesus knows all that is coming upon Him. What does He do?

answers.text: Steps forward and asks who they are looking for
Slips back across the Kidron Valley in the dark
Hides deeper in the garden with His disciples

cards.question: The crowd tells Jesus they are looking for Jesus of Nazareth. True or false: Jesus tells them they have the wrong man.

cards.text: Jesus says, “I am He.” And Judas, His betrayer, is standing right there with the crowd.

cards.question: True or false: When Jesus tells the crowd “I am He,” they draw back and fall to the ground.

cards.text: They brought a whole band of soldiers for ONE man, and they're the ones on the ground. And while they're still dusting off, Jesus asks AGAIN, “Whom are you seeking?”

cards.question: The crowd gives the same answer: Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus says He already told them He is the one. Then what does He ask about His disciples?

answers.text: That the crowd let them go
That the crowd take them too
That the crowd question them first

cards.question: John says Jesus speaking up for His disciples fulfills a word He had spoken before. What was it?

answers.text: I have not lost one of those You have given Me
Those You have given Me will stand with Me to the end
I will lead those You have given Me wherever You send

cards.text: Then Simon Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, draws his sword. He strikes the servant of the high priest and cuts off his right ear.
The servant's name was Malchus, not just 'some servant.' Friend, after years forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, I LOVE seeing a name get remembered.

cards.question: True or false: After Peter cuts off Malchus's ear, Jesus tells Peter to keep his sword out and stand his ground.
Jesus tells Peter to put his sword away. Then He asks if He shouldn't drink the cup the ___ has given Him.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Trust me, friend, this story is FAR from over.

findings.problem: Cards 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13 call the arresting party 'the crowd.' John 18:3 calls them 'a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees.' John never uses the word crowd.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the last item in the verse's list ('lanterns, torches and ___'). The answer is wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. 'Chains' fits an arrest just as well as 'weapons,' so getting it right comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card tells verse 6 ('they're the ones on the ground') as well as verse 7, but it cites only John 18:7. It should cite John 18:6-7.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'John says' appears with no word on who John is. The baker could take him for John the Baptist or for one of the disciples in the garden. He should be introduced simply, as the writer of this Gospel.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
